transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today? Is there something specific that’s been troubling you lately?

Well, hello doctor. Thank you for fitting me in. I, um... I know I’m probably a bit older than the usual folks you see for this sort of thing. I work retail down at the department store, have for years, and you know, you're on your feet all day, you see all sorts of people, and you just want to look presentable. But lately, things have just gotten so out of hand and I didn't know who else to talk to. 

It’s just... well, it started a while ago, and I didn’t think much of it at first. You know how it is, you get stressed, you come home from a long shift, and you just eat a little more than you should. But then I started eating way, way too much. And the guilt—oh, the guilt is just terrible. I just sit there thinking about how my clothes won't fit right, and how I can't afford to gain weight at my age because it's so hard on the knees and the joints, and society is just so cruel to older women who let themselves go. 

And... well, what finally scared me into coming in today, what really made me pick up the phone, is that after I eat too much like that, I’ve been going into the bathroom and making myself throw up. I just do it so I won't gain the weight from all that food. I kept telling myself, you know, that it was just this once, that I was just too full, that it was a mistake. But it isn't just a one-time mistake anymore. It's happening so much more now, and I just feel so ashamed standing over the toilet, trying to keep the bathroom fan on so nobody hears. It's just exhausting me, it really is, and I just can't seem to stop the whole routine once I start worrying about the weight.
How much does your weight or body shape influence how you see yourself or how you feel about yourself?

Oh, doctor, it's... well, it dictates just about everything, to be completely honest with you. I mean, it’s constantly on my mind. Just constantly. 

For instance, you know, working in a department store, we have those big, bright mirrors absolutely everywhere. They're meant to make the displays look nice, but they are just merciless when you're walking past them all day. I'll be walking across the floor, maybe carrying some blouses back to the misses' racks, and if I happen to catch my side view in one of those store mirrors... oh, it just completely ruins my whole day. I just freeze. My heart sinks, and I can't think about anything else for the rest of my shift. 

And it’s not just at work, either. Sundays are supposed to be a day of peace, but getting ready for church has become such a terrible ordeal. If I go to put on one of my nice skirts—even the ones I've worn for years—and it feels even the slightest bit tight around the waist... well, I just spiral. I'll sit there in the pew the entire service, not hearing a single word the pastor says, because I just feel so incredibly self-conscious. I feel like everyone in the congregation is looking at me and they can all tell I’ve let myself go. 

You try to smile and be polite during coffee hour, but inside, I'm just agonizing over how I look and how much space I'm taking up. It’s like my entire mood, my entire sense of whether I'm a decent, presentable person, just completely depends on how my clothes are fitting that morning or what the mirror showed me. It’s exhausting, it really is, spending your whole day pulling at your waistband and hoping nobody is judging you for getting heavy...
